metaData.originalTitle: “尴尬”的智能眼镜，终于不用说“明年是元年了”
metaData.title: "Awkward" Smart Glasses Finally Don't Have to Say "Next Year Is the Year One" Anymore
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Rokid founder Misa stated in an interview that the smart glasses "rocket has ignited" but the tipping point has not arrived; the industry still lacks a killer app, the ecosystem is in its early stages, and future focus should be on repurchase rates rather than market share.
metaData.summary: Based on the speech and in-depth interview of Rokid founder Misa at Rokid Open Day, the article comprehensively examines the latest progress in the smart glasses industry. Misa announced that Rokid's sales grew by 800% year-on-year, with products covering 166 countries and 50-60% of activated users wearing them all day, but he believes the industry is still in the BlackBerry era, with the starting gun yet to be fired. He compared the fundamental route differences between China (AI computing device form factor) and overseas (fashion accessory path), emphasizing that supply chain trust relies on product judgment rather than advance payments and betting agreements. Misa frankly stated that a killer app that is both high-frequency and rigid-demand has not yet been found, and expects to face direct competition from tech giants in 2027. He revealed that Rokid's YodaOS is Agent-centric and may adopt a Token-based billing model in the future, but the ecosystem needs 2 million active users to sustain independent developers. The article also covers privacy controversies, the social and commercial value of accessibility, and globalization and localization strategies, presenting the strategic thinking and practical challenges of a startup in the smart glasses field.

mainPoints.point: The smart glasses industry has crossed the mass production threshold, but still needs a killer app to trigger an explosion.
mainPoints.explanation: Misa used "rocket has ignited" to describe the current stage, but believes that finding an exclusive, high-frequency, and rigid-demand scenario similar to "Fruit Ninja" in the iPhone era is the true iPhone 1 moment.

mainPoints.point: The routes of Chinese and overseas smart glasses are fundamentally different: AI-first vs. Fashion-first.
mainPoints.explanation: Chinese users buy AI capabilities, and the product is an "AI computing device in the form of glasses"; overseas products like Meta Ray-Ban are mainly display-less fashion accessories, and the two paths will not converge in the short term.

mainPoints.point: Supply chain trust is the key to mass production, and product judgment has replaced betting agreements.
mainPoints.explanation: In the early days, Rokid relied on advance payments and betting agreements to gain trust; now, with a clear product roadmap, it has become the center of consensus in the industry chain, reducing supply chain risks.

mainPoints.point: Glasses will not replace the phone, but they will change the phone's role.
mainPoints.explanation: The phone will degenerate into a communication, computing, and storage center, with interaction migrating to the glasses; Rokid has never treated glasses as an accessory since day one, but rather as a challenger to the phone.

mainPoints.point: Current installed base cannot sustain independent developers; 2 million units is the critical point for an ecosystem explosion.
mainPoints.explanation: Rokid expects to reach 2 million active users next year, at which point a standard Token revenue-sharing model will be introduced, and the developer ecosystem can truly start.

keyQuotes: The rocket has already ignited and lifted off, stop questioning whether it will take off.
The winners of the BlackBerry era were not the winners of the iPhone era.
Translation is a rigid demand but not high-frequency, AI Q&A is high-frequency but not a rigid demand; I haven't yet found that product which is both high-frequency and a rigid demand.
Rokid has never treated glasses as an accessory since day one.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Harness Engineering: Finding the Shell That Keeps AI from Going Rogue—Insights from 14 Engineering Articles | Hao's Trend Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of "Harness Engineering," a core technology in the AI Agent field. It reveals how to compensate for model shortcomings through a three-layer management architecture and proposes the logic of "Compensation Surface Migration" that evolves with model capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: 14 Years of Google AI, the Gemini Comeback, and Visual Understanding Models: An Exclusive Interview with Former DeepMind Core Scientist Andrew Dai | Neolabs Special
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: An in-depth interview with former DeepMind core scientist Andrew Dai, reviewing Google AI's 14-year history from missing the GPT moment to the Gemini turnaround, and outlining his vision for founding Elorian AI to explore visual reasoning.

relatedArticles.title: Q1 2026: AI Agents Come of Age | 2026 Q1 AI Trend White Paper
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of four structural trends in AI Agents for Q1 2026: long-horizon productization, harness engineering, recursive R&D, and the Skill ecosystem, revealing the flywheel effect as Agents evolve from tools into independent 'new colleagues'.

relatedArticles.title: 144. A 4-Hour Interview with Yang Meng: Life and Death in Consumer Electronics, Third-Type Companies, AI Variables, Product Methodology, and Choosing Your Game Mode
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anker Innovations founder Yang Meng deeply reviews his 15-year entrepreneurial journey, systematically elaborating on the strategic transformation and methodology from a 'shallow sea' five-series product approach to a 'deep sea' seven-series extreme innovation organization, along with his vision for building an AI-native organization.

relatedArticles.title: In the AI-Induced Cognitive Disarmament, We Will Lose More Than Just Ability | Hao Chat on Trends
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: From the perspectives of cognitive psychology, labor sociology, and philosophy, this article systematically argues that the 'cognitive disarmament' brought about by AI is not a simple degradation of abilities, but a historic turning point where alienation has deepened from the labor process to the thought generation process, rooted in the growth society's endless pursuit of efficiency.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: WWDC26 unveils iOS 27 and new Apple Intelligence developments, upgrading Siri to a system-level AI assistant with its own app, but users in mainland China will temporarily miss out on the AI features.

relatedArticles.title: Kimi Work Beta Invitation: Let Us Share Your Workload
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Kimi launches the beta version of 'Kimi Work', a general-purpose local Agent for knowledge workers, migrating Coding Agent capabilities to a desktop GUI, supporting natural language-driven complex task decomposition, multi-Agent parallel collaboration, and tool invocation.

relatedArticles.title: A Comprehensive Guide to Microsoft Build 2026: The 'Agent-First' Era Arrives with Seven In-House Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Microsoft Build 2026 unveiled seven in-house MAI models, the Scout agent, the MXC system-level security sandbox, and Project Solara, marking the full implementation of an 'Agent-First' strategy.

relatedArticles.title: Why Did Hermes Take Over from OpenClaw in Just Two Months?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth comparison between the rising open-source AI Agent star Hermes and its predecessor OpenClaw, arguing that Hermes' success stems not from functional superiority but from encapsulating decision complexity—such as skill auto-evolution and proactive memory management—within underlying deterministic rules. This engineering safety net allowed it to deliver an automated 'gets better with use' experience precisely when the underlying technology was just barely sufficient.
